{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-md-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"14f9474609f8e7036c56b37afc466a7da415f5df72bea86a636b70f10fc92645","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-md-class-c:lineage:10","source_registry_sha256":"fac6b4b22cda98085a5d7df11947d7cc05865e6c877c17be3df4d573863d1518","source_liveness_sha256":"43fe3511474bec2a914f5cdb112291b78f4339942c4d6fb903d9e3bae34bb3fc"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Basic driving rules","heading":"C — Basic driving: defensive driving, right-of-way, speed, following distance, lanes, turns, passing and parking","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Basic driving: defensive driving, right-of-way, speed, following distance, lanes, turns, passing and parking

FACT_ID: sec03-F01 | anchor: A13
Before driving, carry a valid Learner's Permit or driver's license and the vehicle registration card, adjust your seat and mirrors, and make sure you and every passenger wear a seat belt. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-F02 | anchor: A13
A basic driving rule is that the driver must control the vehicle at all times to avoid a crash, because the driver is responsible for operating it safely. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-F03 | anchor: A13
Defensive driving means constantly watching the front, sides and rear of your vehicle and searching ahead so you are ready to change speed or lanes and have time to spot risks. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-F04 | anchor: A13
To manage risk, adjust speed, position and direction to the road, keep control, give yourself more reaction time, signal your plans, keep a safe gap, and never assume other drivers will do what they should. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-F05 | anchor: A13
Yielding the right-of-way means letting another vehicle, bicyclist or pedestrian go first, and you should never assume you automatically have the right to go first. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-F06 | anchor: A13
Yield to the driver who reaches an intersection before you, and when two drivers arrive at the same time, yield to the driver on your right. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-F07 | anchor: A14
At a four-way intersection with stop signs, yield to the driver on your right, and always yield to pedestrians, bicyclists and drivers still in the intersection. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec03-F08 | anchor: A14
When you stop at a T intersection, yield to drivers already on the through road, and when a yield sign faces you, yield to other drivers. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec03-F09 | anchor: A14
When turning left, yield to drivers in the opposing lane, meaning traffic coming from the opposite direction. [A14]
Why it matters: left-turn yielding is one of the most tested right-of-way rules.
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec03-F10 | anchor: A14
Yield to drivers on the road when you enter it from a driveway or private road, and to drivers already on the highway when you are on an entrance or acceleration ramp. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec03-F11 | anchor: A14
The posted speed limit is the highest legal speed under ideal conditions, and you remain responsible for driving at a safe speed. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec03-F12 | anchor: A14
The safest speed is the pace most traffic is moving, up to the limit, because driving slower than others makes them pass you constantly and raises crash risk. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec03-F13 | anchor: A14
Speeding is one of the most common crash causes: it weakens your handling of curves and obstacles, lengthens stopping, slows hazard recognition, misleads others judging your distance, and increases crash force. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec03-F14 | anchor: A14
Maryland Vehicle Law requires a reasonable speed with awareness of hazards; you may drive below the posted limit for conditions, but driving above it is illegal. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec03-F15 | anchor: A14
Slow down for sharp curves or hills, slippery roads, places with pedestrians or animals, shopping centers, parking lots and downtowns, heavy traffic, narrow bridges and tunnels, toll plazas, schools, playgrounds, residential streets and railroad grade crossings. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec03-F16 | anchor: A14
A railroad grade crossing is a place where the tracks are level with the road. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec03-F17 | anchor: A15
Following too closely causes most rear-end crashes, and the MVA recommends at least 3 to 4 seconds of following distance in ideal conditions. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec03-F18 | anchor: A15
To check your gap, pick a fixed reference point such as a bridge, overpass, sign or mile marker and count from when the car ahead passes it; reaching 3 one thousand before you get there means you are at least 3 seconds back. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec03-F19 | anchor: A15
Behind vehicles that stop often, such as buses and delivery vans, increase your following distance to four or five seconds, or more if needed. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec03-F20 | anchor: A15
Stopping distance depends on how long it takes you to notice danger, the type and condition of the road, your tire tread and your brakes. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec03-F21 | anchor: A15
Drive within a single lane, change lanes only when it is safe, and do not drift over lane lines or change lanes inside an intersection. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec03-F22 | anchor: A15
Keep right of the center of the road unless you are passing a vehicle going your way, a sign or signal permits it, or an obstruction makes moving over necessary. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec03-F23 | anchor: A15
For a turn, watch for turn signs and signals, plan ahead, signal before you reach the turn, look front, back and both sides, and adjust your speed. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec03-F24 | anchor: A15
U-turns are dangerous and not legal everywhere; where allowed, signal left, stop and yield to oncoming traffic, then turn into the outside, right-hand lane going the other way. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec03-F25 | anchor: A16
Before passing, judge the time and space needed, signal, pass at a safe distance, and return to your lane only when both headlights of the passed vehicle show in your rear-view mirror. [A16]
Why it matters: the two-headlights check is the manual's test for a safe return.
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F26 | anchor: A16
Pass on the left as a rule; passing on the right is allowed only when safe and on the road, when the other vehicle is turning left or you are on an unobstructed road or one-way road with two or more lanes in your direction. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F27 | anchor: A16
When another vehicle is passing you, you must yield and must not speed up. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F28 | anchor: A16
Do not pass in a no-passing zone, where the solid yellow center line is on your side, at double solid yellow lines, or when passing would interfere with other vehicles. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F29 | anchor: A16
Do not pass near the top of a hill or on a curve where you cannot see ahead, or with a blocked view within 100 feet of a bridge, elevated road or tunnel. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F30 | anchor: A16
Do not pass while crossing or within 100 feet of an intersection or railroad grade crossing, and never pass on the shoulder on either side. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F31 | anchor: A16
Park only where parking is clearly intended, as far from traffic as possible, and as close to the curb as possible when there is one. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F32 | anchor: A16
After parking, set the parking brake, put a manual car in gear or an automatic in park, check mirrors and traffic before opening the door, and take your keys. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F33 | anchor: A16
Where stay right signs are posted, drive in the right-hand lane or lanes except when passing. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0016]

Glossary: yield the right-of-way — let others go first [A13]. Posted speed limit — the maximum legal speed in ideal conditions [A14]. Reference point — a fixed object used to count following time [A15]. Unobstructed — no median strips, signs or other objects in the way [A16].
Memory aid: count one thousand for each second of gap and aim for at least three before you reach the car ahead's marker [A15].
Misconception: the speed limit is not a target speed; you may legally go slower for conditions but never faster [A14].
